# Source 120 — Federal Register: EO 14409 "Promoting Advanced Artificial Intelligence Innovation and Security"

- **URL:** https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/full_text/html/2026/06/05/2026-11415.html
- **Publisher:** Federal Register (FR Doc. 2026-11415)
- **Published:** 2026-06-05 (order dated June 2, 2026)
- **Type:** Executive Order (official Federal Register text)
- **Status:** fetched 2026-09-14 (full text, http 200)

## Key claims (as stated in source)
- **EO 14409, dated June 2, 2026** (published in the Federal Register June 5, 2026).
- Purpose: promote AI innovation and security by working with the private sector to modernize and harden government/private information systems, protect IP from adversary theft, and cultivate advanced AI-enabled capabilities.
- **Sec. 2 — Upgrading American Systems for Advanced AI:**
  - Within 30 days: Committee on National Security Systems to prioritize cyber defense of National Security Systems; **Secretary of War** to prioritize cyber defense of Department of War information systems; **DHS/CISA** to release Binding Operational Directives expediting cyber defense of civilian Federal systems, expanding AI-enabled defensive tools, and facilitating access to cybersecurity tools including "covered frontier models" for agencies, State/local authorities, and critical-infrastructure operators (rural hospitals, community banks, local utilities).
  - Within 30 days: **Secretary of the Treasury** (with National Cyber Director, NSA, CISA) to form an **AI cybersecurity clearinghouse** (voluntary collaboration with industry) to coordinate/deconflict vulnerability scanning, validate vulnerabilities, and prioritize remediation/patch distribution.
  - Within 30 days: OMB Director to determine Federal grant funding for advanced AI vulnerability detection.
  - Within 60 days: OPM Director to expand US Tech Force Information Cybersecurity Specialist hiring/placement.
- **Sec. 3 — Secure Frontier Model Deployment:** Within 60 days, Treasury/NSA/CISA (with White House, APST, NIST, Commerce) shall:
  - (a) develop/maintain a **classified benchmarking process** to assess advanced cyber capabilities of AI models and set the threshold for designating a **"covered frontier model"** (determination by NSA Director).
  - (b) design a **voluntary framework** with AI developers to: engage the Government on "covered frontier model" designation; provide Government **access to covered frontier models for up to 30 days before release** to trusted partners (under confidentiality/IP protection); and select trusted partners for early access.
  - (c) **Nothing authorizes mandatory governmental licensing, preclearance, or permitting** for development/publication/release/distribution of new AI models, including frontier models.
- **Sec. 4 — Protection Against Criminal Actors:** Attorney General to prioritize enforcement of 18 U.S.C. 1028, 1030, 1343 and other Federal criminal laws against anyone using AI to illegally access/damage computers or to further crimes.

## Verification notes
- Consistent with draft.md usage (EO 14409, June 2 2026, advanced AI innovation and security, "covered frontier model" voluntary pre-release access, no mandatory licensing).
- Primary official Federal Register text — authoritative.
- Note: the order uses "Secretary of War" / "Department of War" (reflecting the 2026 DoD rename).
